notes.title: Good News—and Goodbye!
notes.content: [p]Hi All,[/p][p][/p][p]It’s Liu Zeren, solo creator behind Trance, Trauma. Two years ago, when I made this game, I had no experience developing games whatsoever. There were parts I was proud of and parts I felt really needed improvement. The soundtrack was something I was proud of—I listened to it night after night throughout development.[/p][p]My intention was to create "invisible music," with no distinct melody or rhythm, something that wouldn't draw the player's attention away from the game, but contributed dark ambient textures with a soothing effect. The main theme was composed at the piano and properly notated. But the three rooms' tracks were experimental ambient music built from field recordings, heavily processed into a dark atmosphere. It was a joy to work on all of them.[/p][p]Last month, I rediscovered these tracks, listened again for days, and realized they still moved me as much as they did two years ago. So I’ve decided to release the album. It’s available now on all major platforms (Spotify, Apple Music, NetEase Music, etc.). If you’ve played Trance, Trauma, feel free to look up [i]Trance, Trauma (Original Game Soundtrack)[/i] and give it a listen wherever you are.[/p][p]This is also a goodbye. Trance, Trauma was a guerrilla project pieced together with sticks and stones by a 22-year-old who had no clue what he was doing, and like many solo devs' first projects, it wasn’t very successful. Over the past two years, I’ve improved nonstop and have recently started my second game, something radically different and boldly unique. Releasing this OST is me internally dotting the period on that journey and moving on.[/p][p]Thank you to everyone who gave it a shot.[/p][p][/p][p]—Liu Zeren[/p]
